reason: H0 fuzzes only the default decoder configuration on one compiled platform. It never enables large-window decoding or attaches a shared dictionary, so it cannot reach configuration- and state-dependent paths directly implicated by S1. It also cannot exercise the changed BROTLI_TARGET_64_BITS and BROTLI_UNALIGNED_READ_FAST branches across target builds.
evidence: H0 calls BrotliDecoderCreateInstance followed directly by BrotliDecoderDecompressStream and never sets a decoder parameter; S1 changes BROTLI_STATE_LARGE_WINDOW_BITS and states that BrotliSafeReadBits32Slow is required for "large-window" mode and other extensions.
H0 never calls BrotliDecoderAttachDictionary; S1 changes that function and dictionary-dependent code in CopyFromCompoundDictionary, including brotli_reg_t index and shift handling.
S1 changes bit-reader storage, masks, positions, reads, decoder state fields, and Huffman/distance calculations from uint32_t to brotli_reg_t, whose width is controlled by platform configuration.

S1 removes BROTLI_TARGET_LOONGARCH64 from both BROTLI_TARGET_64_BITS and BROTLI_UNALIGNED_READ_FAST selection, while H0 represents only the behavior of whichever single target configuration builds it.
recommended_action: Add harness variants that enable the large-window decoder parameter, fuzz the BrotliDecoderAttachDictionary-before-decode protocol with independently fuzzed dictionary and stream data, and run the decoder harness under representative 32-bit/64-bit and aligned/unaligned-read compile-time configurations.
